headline: Analysts expect big tech's AI spending growth to slow in 2027, and one researcher estimates the spending will outrun the firms' own cash this year.
score_reason: Analyst forecasts and one research estimate, with the buildout still expected to continue; pool score 6 kept.
importance_line: It matters most to investors and to lenders who may be asked to fund the buildout, since the largest cloud firms may need more outside money, though these are analyst forecasts and one researcher's estimate, not results.
summary: Fortune reports that, on estimates by Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh of Columbia Business School, the capital spending of Oracle, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Alphabet will exceed their combined operating cash flow for the first time in 2026. Pantheon Macroeconomics expects AI-linked investment to keep growing strongly, but expects the largest cloud companies' spending growth to moderate in 2027.
notes: Read in full. Fortune's text is a daily newsletter; only the AI paragraphs are used. The 'AI inflection point' and 'cash-flow negative' terms are the article's; 'operating cash flow' means the cash a firm makes from its own business.
